description: 100 questions on OOP attributes (coding and logic based, intermediate/advanced level)

questions.question: class A: x = 1. Where does x live?
questions.answer: In the class's namespace (A.__dict__) as a class attribute

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self.y = 2. Where does y live?
questions.answer: In each instance's own __dict__ as an instance attribute

questions.question: What is the main difference between a class attribute and an instance attribute?
questions.answer: Class attribute is shared by all instances; instance attribute belongs to one object

questions.question: class A: x = 1. a = A(); b = A(). print(a.x == b.x) outputs?
questions.answer: True (both read the shared class attribute)

questions.question: class A: x = 1. a = A(); b = A(). print(a.x is b.x) outputs?
class A: def __init__(self): self.x = 1. a=A(); b=A(). print(a.x is b.x) outputs?
questions.answer: True for ints (interning), but conceptually each instance stores its own x

questions.question: class A: x = 1. a = A(); a.x = 2. What does a.x return now?
In the setup above, what does A.x return?
class A: x = 1. a=A(); a.x = 2; del a.x. What does a.x return?
class A: x = 1. a=A(); a.x = 2; del a.x. What does A.x return?
class A: x = 1. a=A(); del a.x. What happens?
questions.answer: AttributeError: 'x' is only a class attribute, so there's nothing in the instance to delete

questions.question: class A: data = []. a=A(); b=A(). a.data.append(5); print(b.data) outputs?
class A: data = []. a=A(); a.data = [9]; b=A(). print(b.data) outputs?
questions.answer: [] (a rebinding only touches a's instance, b still sees the class list)

questions.question: class A: data = []. a=A(); a.data.append(1); print(a.data is A.data) outputs?
class A: data = []. a=A(); a.data = a.data + [1]; print(a.data is A.data) outputs?
questions.answer: False (the + rebinds a to a new list)

questions.question: How do you read an attribute whose name is in a string variable?
How do you set an attribute whose name is computed at runtime?
How do you check if an object has an attribute?
What does getattr(obj, 'missing', 42) return when missing isn't present?
What does hasattr(obj, 'missing') return when missing isn't present?
class A: pass. a=A(). What does getattr(a, 'x', 'n/a') return?
class A: x = 10. a = A(). What does getattr(a, 'x') return?
How do you delete an attribute at runtime?
What does delattr(a, 'missing') raise?
What does a.__dict__ show for an object with only instance attributes?
questions.answer: A dictionary mapping attribute names to values

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self.name = 'x'; self.age = 2. print(sorted(A().__dict__)) outputs?
Can you set an attribute directly via the instance __dict__?
class A: pass. a=A(); a.__dict__['z'] = 1; print(a.z) outputs?
What does vars(a) return?
Does the instance __dict__ contain class attributes or methods?
What is the attribute lookup order for obj.name?
questions.answer: obj.__dict__, then the class, then each parent class in MRO, then an exception

questions.question: class A: def method(self): return 1. What is A.Method?
questions.answer: A plain function stored in A.__dict__

questions.question: class A: def method(self): return 1. What does A().method return (without call)?
questions.answer: A bound method (function wrapped with the instance)

questions.question: What does A.__dict__ contain for a class with method m and class attr x?
What does the @property decorator turn a method into?
questions.answer: A read-only 'attribute-like' accessor: obj.prop returns the method's result

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self._v = 1; @property def v(self): return self._v. What does A().v return?
With @property only (no setter), what does a.v = 5 do?
class A: def __init__(self): self._v = 1; @property def v(self): return self._v; @v.setter def v(self, val): self._v = val * 2. What does a = A(); a.v = 5; a._v return?
What does @v.setter allow you to add?
questions.answer: Validation/transformation logic on assignment to the property

questions.question: class A: @property def v(self): return 42; @v.deleter def v(self): raise Exception('no'). What happens on del a.v?
questions.answer: The deleter runs and raises Exception('no')

questions.question: What is the underscore convention _name for?
questions.answer: A soft 'protected' signal: internal, but not enforced

questions.question: What does double-underscore __name do to attribute names?
questions.answer: Name mangling: __name becomes _ClassName__name inside the class

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self.__x = 1. What key is in a.__dict__ for an instance a?
For the setup above, what does a.__x raise?
questions.answer: AttributeError (mangled lookup looks for _A__x only inside class scope)

questions.question: Can you still access the mangled attribute from outside?
questions.answer: Yes, via the full mangled name: a._A__x

questions.question: class A: __x = 5. What does A._A__x return?
class A: def __init__(self): self._v = 1. @property def v(self): return self._v. Is the property on the instance or the class?
class A: x = 1. print(hasattr(A, 'x')) outputs?
class A: x = 1. print(hasattr(A(), 'x')) outputs?
class A: x = 1. print(getattr(A, 'x')) outputs?
What does dir(A()) list?
questions.answer: All accessible attribute/method names, including inherited and dunder ones

questions.question: class A: x = 1. print(sorted([a for a in dir(A()) if not a.startswith('_')])) outputs?
Can two instances of the same class have different sets of attributes?
questions.answer: Yes, attributes can be added per instance

questions.question: class A: pass. a=A(); b=A(). a.z = 1; print('z' in b.__dict__) outputs?
class A: pass. a=A(); print(len(a.__dict__)) outputs?
What does __slots__ = ['x', 'y'] do?
questions.answer: Declares fixed attributes and gives the class no __dict__, saving memory

questions.question: class A: __slots__ = ['x']. a=A(); a.x = 1; print(a.x) outputs?
class A: __slots__ = ['x']. a=A(); a.z = 1 raises what?
questions.answer: AttributeError: 'A' object has no attribute 'z' (slots restrict attributes)

questions.question: class A: __slots__ = ['x']. print(hasattr(A(), '__dict__')) outputs?
questions.answer: False (no instance dict when slots are used)

questions.question: class A: __slots__ = ['x']. print(a.x) before setting returns? (via class default)
questions.answer: It raises AttributeError unless a class-level default exists

questions.question: How do you give reasonable defaults to a slots class?
class A: __slots__ = ['x']; def __init__(self): self.x = 0. What does A().x return?
What are the two main reasons to use __slots__?
questions.answer: Smaller memory footprint and faster attribute access

questions.question: What does a property prevent at Python level?
questions.answer: Direct accidental assignment to a validated/derived attribute

questions.question: class A: x = 1. A.x = 100; print(A().x) outputs?
class A: def __init__(self): self.x = 1; self.x += 1. What does A().x return?
class A: pass. a=A(); setattr(a, 'name', 'n'); print(a.name) outputs?
class A: pass. a=A(); key = 'k'; setattr(a, key, 5); print(a.__dict__) outputs?
class A: x = 1. a=A(). What does a.__getattribute__('x') do?
questions.answer: Runs the default attribute lookup and returns 1

questions.question: What hook is called when an attribute is NOT found normally?
class A: def __getattr__(self, name): return f'missing:{name}'. a=A(); print(a.anything) outputs?
In the setup above, print(a.x) with no attribute x defined outputs?
class A: x = 1; def __getattr__(self, name): return 0. a=A(); print(a.x) outputs?
What does __setattr__ hook do?
questions.answer: Intercepts every attribute assignment for the instance

questions.question: class A: def __setattr__(self, name, value): raise AttributeError('locked'). a=A(); a.x = 1 raises?
In a custom __setattr__, what must you call to actually store an attribute?
class A: def __init__(self): self.x = 1 (plain). Does __getattr__ run for the missing attribute y?
questions.answer: Yes, if __getattr__ is defined, it handles missing y

questions.question: class A: def __delattr__(self, name): raise Exception('blocked'). a=A(); a.x=1; del a.x raises?
How do you compute a derived attribute on the fly?
questions.answer: Use a @property that computes the value from other attributes

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self.v = 10; @property def double(self): return self.v * 2. print(A().double) outputs?
Why call the private-store attribute _v when using a property v?
questions.answer: To avoid infinite recursion (self.v = ... inside the getter would loop)

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self.__v = 1; @property def v(self): return self.__v. print(A().v) outputs?
What does 'x' in dir(A) return for a class attribute x?
class A: x = 1; def m(self): return 2. print('m' in dir(A), 'x' in dir(A)) outputs?
class A: x = 1. print('x' in A.__dict__) outputs?
class A: def m(self): return 1. print('m' in A.__dict__) outputs?
What does A.__name__, A.__qualname__ refer to?
questions.answer: Strings holding the class's name/qualified name

questions.question: class A: pass. What does A.__dict__.keys() result show?
class A: x = 1. a=A(). What does getattr type manipulation a.__dict__.update({'y': 2}) do?
questions.answer: Adds attribute y to the instance: a.y becomes 2

questions.question: class A: x = 1. Can you read a class attribute through an instance?
questions.answer: Yes, a.x works if no instance x shadows it

questions.question: class A: x = [1]. a = A(); a.x[0] = 99. print(A.x) outputs?
questions.answer: [99] (mutating, not rebinding, affects the shared list)

questions.question: class A: x = {'k': 1}. a=A(); a.x['k'] = 2. print(A().x) outputs?
class A: def __init__(self): self.x = 1. a=A(); print(sorted(vars(a))) outputs?
What does a class attribute update do to existing instances?
questions.answer: They see the new value unless they have their own shadowing instance attribute

questions.question: class A: x = 1. a=A(); a.x = 2; A.x = 99. print(a.x, A().x) outputs?
questions.answer: 2 99 (a is shadowed; new instance uses class value)

questions.question: class A: x = 1. What is the safest way to add validation to x assignments?
questions.answer: Make x a property with a setter and store the raw value in _x

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self.x = 1. print(A().__dict__ == {'x': 1}) outputs?
How do you detect that an attribute exists on the class but not the instance?
questions.answer: 'x' in type(obj).__dict__ and 'x' not in obj.__dict__

questions.question: class A: x = 1. a=A(). print('x' in a.__dict__, 'x' in type(a).__dict__) outputs?
class A: def __init__(self): self.x = [1]. a=A(); b=A(). Are a.x and b.x the same object?
questions.answer: No, the constructor creates a fresh list for each instance
